JUDGEMENT CALLS
S11 (391,504) - OVERRIDDEN junction -> crossing. At 10x the x~391 column makes an unmistakable semicircular hop, bulging right to x~400 between y~487 and y~522, exactly the same S-jog the drafter used at S6. The tracer's hop score (2.1) is fooled because the skeleton splits the arc across a second, deg-2 site at (382,490). Taking it as a junction would have fused the #2/#8/#12 gate column with the Zener/#3-gate/#6-gate column into one 7-terminal net, i.e. every gate on the sheet plus both AC sources on a single node, and would contradict the drafter's own convention on this sheet.
S6 (392,366) - kept the default crossing. Identical S-jog, unambiguous at 10x (arc from (388,349) to (386,384), bulging to x~403).
S5 (553,366) - plain X, no dot (dot=1.6, i.e. stroke width), no hop. At 10x both strokes run straight through; the ~3 px lateral wobble of the vertical near y~355 is pen tremor, an order of magnitude smaller than the 15-20 px arcs at S6/S11. Read as a JUNCTION per the ink prior (this drafter draws an explicit jog when he means 'not connected', and he did so twice on this sheet). The alternative reading, crossing, is also electrically sane - it would split n3 into {#2 source, #6 drain} and {#3 source, #5 drain}, two 2-terminal nets - so this one rests on the ink prior plus the drafter's demonstrated habit, not on an impossibility argument.
S14 (563,623) - deg=4 only because of the small arrow-like tick the drafter put under the resistor's left lead at (568,633). The lead itself plainly terminates on the x~563 vertical, which runs straight through: junction.
S0, S1, S8, S9, S12, S15, S31, S33, S34, S35, S36, S37 - all plain T's in which one run visibly ends on the other; junction, confirmed individually in the site crops.

PIN ORDER (drain, gate, source) - checked on all six MOSFETs at 8x
The gate is the isolated lead facing the separate vertical gate bar. Drain vs source was settled from the ink, not from a supply/ground heuristic: in every MOSFET on this sheet the middle (bulk) stub, the one carrying the arrowhead, is tied by a short vertical to the BOTTOM lead, with a clear gap to the top lead's vertical. Bottom lead = source, top lead = drain, on all six.
